nodes.name: HPHT synthesis of pyrite sulfides
nodes.procedure: Fe-doped CoS2 (Co0.8Fe0.2S2, referred to as Fe-CoS2), Ni-doped CoS2 (Co0.8Ni0.2S2, referred to as Ni-CoS2), Fe- and Ni-codoped CoS2 (Co0.8Fe0.11Ni0.09S2, referred to as Fe,Ni-CoS2), and pristine CoS2, FeS2, and NiS2 are synthesized under high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) conditions (see the Experimental Section in the Supporting Information for details).
nodes.source_text: Fe-doped CoS2 (Co0.8Fe0.2S2, referred to as Fe-CoS2), Ni-doped CoS2 (Co0.8Ni0.2S2, referred to as Ni-CoS2), Fe- and Ni-codoped CoS2 (Co0.8Fe0.11Ni0.09S2, referred to as Fe,Ni-CoS2), and pristine CoS2, FeS2, and NiS2 are synthesized under high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) conditions (see the Experimental Section in the Supporting Information for details).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe,Ni-CoS2, Ni-CoS2, and Fe-CoS2 exhibit pyrite-type structure (Space group: Pa3) without impurity peaks; (200) plane shift indicates successful Fe/Ni doping; Rietveld refinement gives lattice parameter 5.535 Å for Fe,Ni-CoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained XRD patterns of Fe,Ni-CoS2, Fe-CoS2, and Ni-CoS2 (Figure 1a) can be indexed into a pyrite-type structure (Space group: Pa3) without distinguishable impurity. The observed difference of the (200) plane... indicating the successful doping of Fe or/and Ni into CoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoS2 shows Raman modes Eg (288 cm-1), Tg(1) (312 cm-1), Ag (390 cm-1), Tg(2) (414 cm-1); Fe,Ni-CoS2 similar with slight red shift; Ni-CoS2 blue shift; Fe-CoS2 red shift; distinctive Ag peak confirms homogeneous single-phase sulfides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman modes of CoS2, Eg (288 cm-1), Tg(1) (312 cm-1), Ag (390 cm-1), and Tg(2) (414 cm-1), are observed... The distinctive Ag peak suggests that the obtained Fe,Ni-CoS2, Ni-CoS2, and Fe-CoS2 are homogeneous single-phase sulfides.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals common interacting nanoparticle features ranging from tens to hundreds of nanometers for the catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Figure S3) reveals common interacting nanoparticle features (ranging from tens to hundreds of nanometers).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX analysis finds very uniform composition distributions and stoichiometric ratio of CoS2, Ni-CoS2, Fe-CoS2, and Fe,Ni-CoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis finds very uniform composition distributions and the stoichiometric ratio of CoS2, Ni-CoS2, Fe-CoS2, and Fe,Ni-CoS2, as shown in Figure S4 and Table S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows clear lattice fringe of 0.32 nm corresponding to the (111) crystal plane of pyrite Fe,Ni-CoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images (Figure S5) show a clear lattice fringe of 0.32 nm, corresponding to the (111) crystal plane of pyrite Fe,Ni-CoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDX compositional mapping indicates homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, Ni, and S constituents.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the compositional mapping from TEM-EDX (Figure S5) also indicates the homogeneous distribution of the constituents (Fe, Co, Ni, and S).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe,Ni-CoS2 has charge transfer resistance Rct of 6.87 Ω, smaller than other sulfides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, Fe,Ni-CoS2 has a smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct, 6.87 Ω) than those of other sulfides (Fe-CoS2 39.3 Ω, Ni-CoS2 97.9 Ω, CoS2 323 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of Fe,Ni-CoS2 is 9.39 mF cm-2, higher than Fe-CoS2 (6.48 mF cm-2), Ni-CoS2 (9.23 mF cm-2), and CoS2 (8.07 mF cm-2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value of Fe,Ni-CoS2 is 9.39 mF cm-2 (Figure S8e), higher than those of Fe-CoS2 (6.48 mF cm-2) Ni-CoS2 (9.23 mF cm-2), and CoS2 (8.07 mF cm-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows increased O 1s peak intensity after OER, suggesting more oxidized species formed on Fe,Ni-CoS2 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As compared with the original Fe,Ni-CoS2 the peak intensity of O 1s after OER is much greater (Figure S10), which suggests that more oxidized species were formed on the surface during the OER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows Ag peak of Fe,Ni-CoS2 disappears at 1.45 V (vs 1.65 V for CoS2); CoOOH peaks emerge at 480 and 600 cm-1; Ni evolves to β-Ni(OH)2 at 448 cm-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the Ag peak of Fe,Ni-CoS2 (Figure 3a) disappears completely at 1.45 V, which is much lower than that of CoS2 (1.65 V), indicating that Fe and Ni codoping facilitates the dynamic surface reconstruction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Co, Fe, Ni K-edge XANES show similar evolution; Fe,Ni codoping promotes faster Co/Fe oxidation to high-valence oxyhydroxides while suppressing Ni oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Co (c), Fe (d), and Ni (e) K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Fe,Ni-CoS2 at varied potentials during the OER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Co, Fe, Ni K-edge XANES of Fe,Ni-CoS2 show progressive increase in features B and C at expense of A; Fe,Ni codoping accelerates Co/Fe oxidation to high-valence oxyhydroxides vs single doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Co (c), Fe (d), and Ni (e) K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Fe,Ni-CoS2 at varied potentials during the OER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS-FT shows Co-S (1.90 Å) and Co-M (3.53 Å) peaks weaken with potential increase; CoOOH peaks (Co-O 1.45 Å, Co-Co 2.42 Å) develop rapidly 1.3-1.4 V; coordination number Co-S decreases, Co-O increases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS-FT results of Co K-edge for Fe,Ni-CoS2 (Figure 4c) show that the Co-S (at about 1.90 Å) and Co-M peaks (M = Fe, Co, and Ni at about 3.53 Å) weaken as the potential increases.
